questions.question: How many orthologous core genes and genomes were used in the maximum-likelihood tree?
questions.rationale: The results specify 662 orthologs per genome and 114 genomes in the tree.
questions.evidence_quote: A total of thirty-two Anoxybacillus, seventy-three Geobacillus, eight Parageobacillus and one Bacillus genomes (Supplementary Table S1 ) produced a core gene set of 662 orthologous genes per genome, which was used to produce a maximum likelihood phylogenetic tree with 114 genomes.

questions.question: What was the broad division of genera across clades I and II?

options.A: Clade I contained all Geobacillus, all Parageobacillus and some Anoxybacillus; clade II contained most Anoxybacillus.
options.B: All Anoxybacillus fell in I and both other genera in II.

questions.rationale: The combined core tree and ANI/AAI dendrograms showed this two-clade pattern.
questions.evidence_quote: The combined results from the core gene tree and ANI and AAI dendrograms show that the genomes split into two main clades, clade I containing all Geobacillus, all Parageobacillus and some species of Anoxybacillus, and clade II, containing the majority of Anoxybacillus species.

questions.question: Which taxonomic proposal did the authors make for clade I-c?

options.A: Place A. tepidamans and one genomospecies in the new genus Quasigeobacillus.
options.B: Transfer every Anoxybacillus species into Geobacillus.
options.C: Merge clade I-c into Parageobacillus without qualification.
options.D: Retain all clade I-c taxa in Anoxybacillus.

questions.rationale: The core gene tree and ANI/AAI evidence led to proposal of a distinct genus for the two clade-I-c taxa.
questions.evidence_quote: Considering the evidence of the core gene maximum likelihood tree, ANI and AAI UPGMA dendrograms and similarity values, we suggest that A. tepidamans and the one genomospecies present in clade I-c should be placed into a new genus called Quasigeobacillus.

questions.question: Why were the affinities of A. vitaminiphilus and A. amylolyticus left unresolved?

options.A: Their positions were incongruent across the trees/methods.

questions.rationale: The authors state that inconsistent placement across analyses prevented resolution.
questions.evidence_quote: Due to the incongruous positioning of A. vitaminiphilus and A. amylolyticus the affinities of these two species remains unresolved at this point.

questions.question: How many assemblies were removed during core-gene discovery, and why?

options.A: Six: five low-CDS assemblies reduced the recognized core set, and one was an exact duplicate.
options.D: Seven assemblies, one per focal genus.

questions.rationale: The exclusions comprised five low-CDS assemblies plus one duplicate Anoxybacillus strain.
questions.evidence_quote: During the core gene discovery process, five assemblies with relatively low numbers of CDS were excluded after they were found to significantly reduce the number of core genes recognised, and one was removed as it was an exact duplicate of another Anoxybacillus Suryakundensis strain.

questions.question: Which outgroup was used in the core-gene analysis?
questions.rationale: The methods explicitly identify B. subtilis spizizenii as the outgroup; NG80-2 was the starting reference.
questions.evidence_quote: The genome assembly of Bacillus subtilis spizizenii TU-B-10T [54] was included in the core gene analysis as an outgroup.

questions.question: How many candidate CDS were found unique to clade I-c?
questions.rationale: The comparative BLASTn analysis identified six candidate CDS as clade-I-c-specific.
questions.evidence_quote: A total of 6 CDS were found to be unique to clade I-c.

questions.question: What evidence concern argued against simply merging the new clade into Parageobacillus?

options.A: That would also support merging Parageobacillus back into Geobacillus.
options.D: The clade was already in clade II.

questions.rationale: The authors reasoned the phylogenetic evidence would not support a simple merger without a broader taxonomic consequence.
questions.evidence_quote: An alternative approach may be to merge these two species with Parageobacillus; however, if this course of action was followed, the evidence from the phylogenetic trees would also support the need for Parageobacillus to be merged again with Geobacillus.

questions.question: What distinction between the dataset and tree explains 113 versus 114 genome counts?

options.A: 113 focal genomes were selected, with a Bacillus outgroup added for a 114-genome tree.
options.B: 114 focal genomes became 113 after outgroup exclusion.
options.C: Both counts refer to core genes.
options.D: 113 genomes were used for the tree and 114 for ANI only.

questions.rationale: The abstract counts 113 focal genomes; the phylogenetic tree includes the added Bacillus outgroup.
questions.evidence_quote: A total of 113 genomes were selected for phylogenomic metrics including calculation of Average Nucleotide Identity (ANI) and Average Amino acid Identity (AAI)

questions.question: What broad taxonomic sampling lesson do the authors emphasize for assigning new genomes?

options.A: Analyze closely related species together to avoid genus assignments that conflict with the broader phylogeny.
options.B: Use only 16S because whole-genome analyses obscure relationships.
options.C: Assign a genus from the single nearest genome without phylogenetic context.
options.D: Avoid ANI and AAI when genera are closely related.

questions.rationale: The conclusion warns that analysis without broader phylogenetic context can yield incongruent genus designations.
questions.evidence_quote: In the context of determining affinities of a new genome, it is essential to consider closely related species together for construction of a phylogeny. When this process occurs in the absence of a broader phylogenetic assessment, the genus designation for new strains can become incongruent with the phylogeny of the underlying complete set of available genomes.
